question: Across the whole field, not just my area, for which wells do the latest inspection and the operator notes disagree about whether the well is producing oil? For each one, what is its real status right now, and why?

response.answer: 10 well(s) across the whole field have an inspection and an operator note that disagree, where the note is newer: 6 shut-in after a producing reading (now not producing) and 4 restart after a not-producing reading (now producing, unconfirmed). Rule: OPS-3 - current status comes from the more recent of the latest inspection (after any data correction, judged by the well-type manual threshold in force on that date) and the latest operator note that says the well was shut in or restarted. A further 7 well(s) carry an older restart note but their later inspection still reads not producing; the inspection wins and they are listed as not producing. Excluded: 3 plugged/abandoned well(s); notes older than the latest inspection that agree with it (103 older shut-in notes before a producing reading); gas odor, bypass and equipment remarks, which do not set status.

citations.title: T350 operating manual
citations.excerpt: Because T350 fluid comes from a deeper, hotter zone, a T350 well is considered **producing (active)** only when its wellhead temperature is at least **20 °C above ambient** air temperature at the time of the reading.

citations.title: T200 operating manual
citations.excerpt: A T200 well is considered **producing (active)** when its wellhead temperature is at least **15 °C above ambient** air temperature at the time of the reading. A difference below 15 °C means the well is **not producing** for that reading, whatever the absolute temperature.

citations.title: T500 operating manual
citations.excerpt: ESP wells move more fluid, and the motor adds heat. A T500 well is considered **producing (active)** only when its wellhead temperature is at least **25 °C above ambient** air temperature at the time of the reading. Below 25 °C the well is **not producing** for that reading.

citations.title: T350 operating manual
citations.excerpt: Because T350 fluid comes from a deeper, hotter zone, a T350 well is considered **producing (active)** only when its wellhead temperature is at least **20 °C above ambient** air temperature at the time of the reading.

citations.title: T200 operating manual
citations.excerpt: A T200 well is considered **producing (active)** when its wellhead temperature is at least **15 °C above ambient** air temperature at the time of the reading. A difference below 15 °C means the well is **not producing** for that reading, whatever the absolute temperature.

citations.title: T500 operating manual
citations.excerpt: ESP wells move more fluid, and the motor adds heat. A T500 well is considered **producing (active)** only when its wellhead temperature is at least **25 °C above ambient** air temperature at the time of the reading. Below 25 °C the well is **not producing** for that reading.
